replies.text: {"verdicts":[{"id":"T1","keep":true,"reason":"Design confirms offline cache of notes/history on shared tablets; unbounded retention is a concrete disclosure risk."},{"id":"T2","keep":true,"reason":"Shared devices with local cache; absence of auth before patient data is a concrete spoofing attack."},{"id":"T3","keep":true,"reason":"Offline sync of edits is in design; tampering with queued SQLite records is concrete."},{"id":"T4","keep":true,"reason":"Shared devices plus offline edits support non-attributable clinical notes; distinct harm from T2/T3."},{"id":"T5","keep":true,"reason":"Offline sync implies conflict resolution; silent overwrite of clinical history is concrete and distinct."},{"id":"T6","keep":true,"reason":"Offline operation requires pre-fetch; over-broad caching/identifier manipulation beyond assignment is concrete."}]}
